decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom represents substantial development investment and a publicly announced Q1/2019 release, so the firm is strongly committed to it and any slow uptake can be attributed to the pending launch.
Small volume chambers are core to the firm's decades-long dosimetry identity and need little upkeep, so dropping one so soon after launch would contradict the firm's own recent decision.
This chamber sits within the established dosimetry portfolio and is visibly presented on its own page, so the firm will persist with it while it builds market adoption.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is central to the firm's calibration and measurement business, which makes withdrawal highly unlikely only a year after launch.
Relative dosimetry chambers complement the firm's water phantoms and QA workflow, and the launch investment and public commitment favor keeping it.
Thimble chambers are a staple of the firm's dosimetry line, and with no evidence of failure, management will justify its recent launch by retaining it.
